purpose: survive the log's lost tail: mirror every motion probe line into an SD-card breadcrumb file, so the call the thread dies in can be read even though Skyline's TCP log stops a few lines short

why_breadcrumbs.reading: each report ended mid-sequence, a few lines before the fault: the crashing call's own '[motionbind] BEFORE' line (p8), the '[articlescope] STATE' line plus 'FORCE restored' (p10). The game kills the thread inside call_original, and Skyline's log is a TCP stream (skyline::logging::log -> skyline_tcp_send_raw) with no flush before the thread dies.
why_breadcrumbs.sink: std::fs writes to the SD card already work in this engine (kind_ledger writes sd:/ultimate/clone_engine/kinds.txt), so the same lines are written as they are produced; the file's last line is the call that died

p10_result.evidence: the p9 fault at cross2 + 0x49748c (the patch site, a plain store the game rejected) is gone; the report then shows four weapon motion setups finishing with holders created
p10_result.new_fault: main + 0x4984d4: 'ldr x8, [x19, #0x10]' (holder) -> 'ldr x0, [x8, #0x10]' (holder+0x10) -> vtable+0x38 called with x1=0 -> returned 0 -> 'ldr x8, [x0]' dereferences the null. X08 = holder, X20 = 0.
p10_result.still_unknown: which module/bind that call belonged to, because its own log lines were the ones lost

breadcrumb_lines: [bind] enter module=... kind=... lr=@... res=... count=... holder=... head=[+0x8,+0x10,+0x18,+0x50] state_obj=... vt=... +0x256=... first=... [FORCE-CANDIDATE]
[bind] exit lr=@... res ...->... holder ...->... head=[...] - written only when the call returned
[force] refused | applied | nop verified | failed | restored module=...
[setup] enter object=... kind=... boma=... module=... mkind=... holder=... res=... count=... state_obj=... vt=... method=@... +0x38=... +0x256=... flags=[...] [CRASH-PRECONDITION]
[setup] exit object=... kind=... module=... holder ...->... - a setup whose enter has no exit is the weapon the thread died inside
diagnostics_added: every [bind] call is breadcrumbed, not just first sight, so a repeat call cannot hide
holder head words at bind entry and exit, so a forced holder can be compared with a naturally created one
weapon motion setup enter/exit pair, so the dying weapon kind is identifiable without the TCP tail
[setup] enter carries the STATE fields behind a 48-line gate instead of 24
